Practical automation

Your first automation: start with one useful task

Choose a repeated task, define a useful result and give someone responsibility for checking it. Build confidence before adding more.

AP Tech Agency3 min read23 November 2026

In this guide

Choose a task you can explainDefine what it can and cannot doUse AI where it has a clear roleTest the less obvious situationsCheck whether it helps your team

Choose a task you can explain

Look for work your team repeats in a similar way: collecting enquiry details, preparing a summary or drafting an answer from approved information. Choose a task with a clear starting point and a result someone can check.

Write down the steps. If they change every time, settle the process first. You will have a clearer idea of what to automate and where a person needs to decide.

Define what it can and cannot do

Decide what starts the process, which information it can use and what it should produce. Name the tools involved and the person responsible. Set approval rules for actions such as sending messages or changing customer records. A first version can simply prepare a draft.

For example, an enquiry process might collect the submitted details, flag anything missing and prepare an internal note. A team member can review the note and choose the next action. Describe that result before building.

Use AI where it has a clear role

A simple rule may be enough to place a completed form in the right list. AI can help summarise a message or prepare a draft reply. Give each step a clear purpose and decide how a person will review work that needs judgement.

Test the less obvious situations

Try missing details, unclear wording, duplicate enquiries and requests outside the process. Decide when the automation should pause and ask for help. Keep a record of what happened so the responsible person can find and correct a problem.

Check whether it helps your team

Look at the work the automation creates as well as the work it removes. How much checking does it need? Does the result help someone take the next step? Use your team’s examples to improve it.

Include tool costs, access permissions and ongoing maintenance in the plan. Once the first task works as intended, review whether another step is worth adding. Keep each new action clear so your team can stay in control.

Turn an idea into a plan.

Tell us what you want to achieve and where you need help. Start with a few details in our project brief.
